For users in the United States looking for the best free podcast maker, several excellent tools offer robust features for recording, editing, and hosting. The ideal choice often depends on your operating system, specific needs (e.g., solo recording, remote interviews), and desired level of editing control.

Here are some of the top free podcast-making tools:

### **For Recording & Editing**

*   **Audacity**
    *   **Description:** Audacity is a widely popular, open-source digital audio workstation (DAW) that is completely free and runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It offers powerful multi-track recording and editing capabilities, making it a go-to for many professional podcasters who started out. You can record, clean, cut, and export your audio, and it supports various audio formats and plugins.
    *   **Pros:** Unlimited features with no time limits or watermarks, excellent for solo recording and comprehensive editing, and includes noise reduction tools.
    *   **Cons:** Its user interface can appear dated.
    *   **Best for:** Solo creators who need advanced editing features and are comfortable with a desktop application.

*   **GarageBand**
    *   **Description:** For Apple users, GarageBand comes pre-installed on every Mac, iPhone, and iPad, offering a surprisingly capable podcast production studio. It provides a more visual interface with built-in sound effects and a library of royalty-free loops and jingles.
    *   **Pros:** Free for Apple users, user-friendly interface, multi-track recording, basic effects, and a good option for a more visual workflow.
    *   **Cons:** Exclusively for Apple devices.
    *   **Best for:** Mac and iOS users who want a straightforward and capable tool for recording and editing.

*   **Riverside.fm**
    *   **Description:** Riverside.fm is a browser-based platform designed for high-quality audio and video recording, especially useful for remote interviews. Its free plan offers two hours of separate track recording for both audio and video, capturing high-quality files locally on each participant's computer.
    *   **Pros:** Excellent for remote guest interviews with high-quality local recording, supports video podcasting.
    *   **Cons:** The free tier has time limitations.
    *   **Best for:** Podcasters conducting interviews with remote guests.

*   **Spotify for Podcasters (formerly Anchor)**
    *   **Description:** This all-in-one platform is completely free and handles basic editing, hosting, and distribution. It supports both audio and video podcasting with unlimited uploads, advanced analytics, and monetization options.
    *   **Pros:** Completely free for hosting and distribution, easy to use, supports video podcasts, and offers creation tools.
    *   **Cons:** Editing capabilities are more basic compared to dedicated DAWs.
    *   **Best for:** Beginners looking for an all-in-one solution for creating, hosting, and distributing their podcast for free.

*   **Podcastle**
    *   **Description:** Podcastle is a simple method to make a podcast and offers a free tier for recording and editing. It also assists with transcribing interviews and repurposing content.
    *   **Pros:** User-friendly, good for recording remote guests and transcriptions.
    *   **Cons:** Free tier may have limitations on features or usage.
    *   **Best for:** Those seeking an easy-to-use browser-based tool, especially for interviews.

*   **CapCut**
    *   **Description:** CapCut offers a free podcast maker that allows real-time voice-overs and extensive editing tools for both audio and video content. You can adjust volume, pitch, speed, and quality, and even remove and replace video backgrounds.
    *   **Pros:** Free, versatile for both audio and video podcasts, real-time recording, and comprehensive editing features.
    *   **Cons:** May be more focused on video editing, which might be overkill for audio-only podcasts.
    *   **Best for:** Creators who want to produce video podcasts and need a tool for both audio and visual editing.

### **For Hosting & Distribution**

While many recording/editing tools offer some form of direct publishing, dedicated hosting platforms ensure your podcast is accessible across all major listening apps.

*   **Spotify for Creators (formerly Anchor)**
    *   **Description:** As mentioned above, it's a completely free platform that includes unlimited hosting and distribution to major platforms like Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and more.
    *   **Pros:** Fully free hosting, unlimited uploads, broad distribution, and analytics.
    *   **Cons:** Might lack advanced features found in paid hosting services.
    *   **Best for:** Anyone needing a free, comprehensive solution for hosting and getting their podcast everywhere.

*   **RSS.com**
    *   **Description:** RSS.com offers free podcast hosting with unlimited episodes and audio. It simplifies distribution by automatically sending your podcast to major platforms like Spotify, Apple Podcasts, YouTube, and Amazon Music.
    *   **Pros:** Truly free podcast hosting with unlimited audio and episodes, easy distribution, and monetization options.
    *   **Cons:** While hosting is free, other features or higher-tier analytics might be paid.
    *   **Best for:** Podcasters looking for genuinely free hosting with unlimited content and wide distribution.

*   **Podbean**
    *   **Description:** Podbean provides a free podcast hosting service, allowing you to record and publish podcasts using their app.
    *   **Pros:** Free plan available, user-friendly for uploading and sharing, and offers tools for creation, promotion, and monetization.
    *   **Cons:** Free plan has limitations on storage space and features compared to paid plans.
    *   **Best for:** Beginners who want a reputable hosting service with a free entry point.

*   **Buzzsprout**
    *   **Description:** Buzzsprout offers a free tier for podcast hosting, known for its simplicity and ease of use, particularly for beginners.
    *   **Pros:** Excellent for beginners, user-friendly interface, and good for basic hosting and distribution.
    *   **Cons:** The free plan has limitations on upload time per month and episode retention.
    *   **Best for:** New podcasters who prioritize ease of use and a straightforward hosting experience.

In summary, for powerful and flexible *editing*, **Audacity** (for all operating systems) and **GarageBand** (for Apple users) are excellent free choices. For *remote interviews*, **Riverside.fm** offers a generous free tier for high-quality recording. For a comprehensive *all-in-one solution* for creation, hosting, and distribution, **Spotify for Podcasters** is highly recommended due to its complete freeness and robust features. If your primary need is *free hosting with unlimited content*, **RSS.com** stands out.
